 Suspectives is the first game announced for The Jackbox Party Pack 11 . It is a social deduction game where players have to figure out the secret criminal based on their answers to a survey.

 Gameplay [ ] 

 You start the game by answering a 8-question survey, which includes 7 multiple-choice questions and a fill-in-the-blank question. After everyone submit their answers, a crime is revealed (related to one of the survey questions) and a player becomes the secret criminal.

 Then, the remaining 7 evidence (the criminal's answers to the remaining questions) will be revealed one at a time, along with the number of players that give the same answer. If that is not everyone, they will publicly vote on which player(s) could the evidence describe. After that, one player is chosen to interrogate a player of their choice, while others vote on how suspicious the interrogated player is.

 However, one of the evidence is phony, written by a player who is not the criminal. Therefore after the third and sixth rounds, the lie detector can be used. Players vote on which evidence they want to inspect: If the evidence is phony, it is removed; Otherwise the players can vote to see a player's answer to the related category.

 After all evidence is revealed (or when the players skip to the final verdict), the players have 2 votes to vote for their top suspects: players receiving no votes are out of consideration. They can then cast the final vote on who they think the criminal is. If the final vote is tied (no verdict) or the player receiving the most votes is not the criminal, the criminal escapes; Otherwise the criminal is convicted.

 Suspectives (stylized as SUSPECTIVES ) is a social deduction video game and one of five games featured in The Jackbox Party Pack 11 .

 In this game, players answer survey questions, whose answers become evidence for a crime that was committed, and they have to figure out who the criminal is based on those responses.

 Gameplay

 Each game begins with players answering some quick survey questions, ranging from topics like "What's a favorite toy you had growing up?" and "Have you worn a hat today?"

 After all the answers are submitted, word goes out that a crime has been committed, with only one player being the secret criminal. (Players would check their device to see if they're the criminal.) However, as each piece of evidence is revealed, players must keep in mind that only one piece is phony . 

 Each piece of evidence is relayed one at a time, as well as how many players in the party answered the survey's answer shown. If one or more player(s) answered in the way shown (such as 2 players answering with "perp likes their coffee with milk and sugar" for example), everyone can pin guesses on who it could be. If everyone chose the same one (like "perp is confident that they can install a TV"), no guesses are able to be placed. A player is then chosen to interrogate one of the others and everyone votes on whether they think the player is innocent or suspicious.

 At any point, players can hit a READY TO SOLVE button if they're confident they know who the criminal is. Only a majority vote can allow the party to skip straight to the accusation, but you can't turn back once you're ready, so it should not be taken lightly.

 After a few pieces of evidence are played, a Lie Detector is able to be used by the party, putting a piece of evidence in play and determining whether it's real or fake. If it's real, you get to reveal one player's honest answer to that survey. If a person's answer doesn't match the survey answer, they are deemed "cleared". If it's phony, it's crossed out and everyone gets back to the game with the next piece of evidence.

 During the final verdict, every player has two votes to cast suspicion then one vote to accuse. If the party ties, there is no verdict and the criminal escapes. Otherwise, a majority can result in either a guilty verdict or an innocent verdict depending on the guess.

 Development

 The game's basic premise was first unveiled during the Jackbox Games Direct on April 7th, 2025 [ 1 ] , where it was also revealed that the game would be directed by Tim Sniffen , who previously directed Tee K.O. 2 , Fakin' It All Night Long , and The Jackbox Survey Scramble .

 The game's title was announced as Suspectives on May 5th, 2025. [ 2 ] From June 14th to July 29th, eight of the dog avatars were revealed. [ 3 ] [ 4 ] 

 The first full gameplay was revealed during PAX West on September 1st, where it was also revealed that Elise Wattman is the game's composer. [ 5 ] 

 The design team for the game are as follows:
